title: Little brothers
hook: the friars minor, the lesser brothers

segments.voice: Yesterday, the gospel as the rule: Francis heard Jesus send the twelve out with nothing, and did it. Your line was take nothing.

Names for leaders tend to climb. Manager, senior manager, director, vice president, chief. Every title is a step up, and everyone can see who's where. Francis's small band of followers needed a name. Some readers hear in his choice an echo of the Italian towns of his day, where, they say, the powerful were called the major people and everyone else the minor people. Either way, Francis picked the low side, and he put it right in the name. Today's word: friar.
screen: `TITLES THAT CLIMB.` → `THE MAJOR AND THE MINOR.` → `FRANCIS PICKS THE LOW SIDE.`

segments.voice: Friar simply means brother. Francis's companions were the fratres minores: the lesser brothers, the little brothers. That's still the official name, the Order of Friars Minor. His early biographer tells how it happened. When the words of the rule were being written and they came to the phrase, let them be lesser, Francis said: I want this brotherhood to be called the Order of Lesser Brothers. In the earliest rule the brothers kept, the idea runs all the way through. Nobody is to be called prior, which means the one who comes first. All are lesser brothers, and they wash one another's feet. Even those put in charge are called ministers, which means servants. It echoes a gospel scene. The disciples argue about which of them is the greatest, and Jesus answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "But you not so: but he that is the greater among you, let him become as the younger; and he that is the leader, as he that serveth." Friars are also a different shape of religious life from the monks who promise stability. They don't live behind a monastery wall for good. They go out, into towns and along roads, among ordinary people, preaching, working, begging when they must. Monks stay; friars move. The Church recognizes both as ways of giving a life to God. But a friar's whole identity starts from below: lesser, by choice, and brother, to everyone.

segments.voice: Think of one place where you usually take the higher seat, the one who decides, who speaks first, who's right, and without putting yourself down, picture standing there as a brother or sister instead of a boss. Asking instead of telling, serving instead of directing, hearing out the person you'd usually overrule. If you pray, hold the gospel line: he that is the leader, as he that serveth.
Friar. Brother: a member of an order like Francis's lesser brothers, the friars minor, who live out among people rather than behind a monastery wall. Today's word.

notes: 'Friar simply means brother' — a word origin (Latin frater, via Old French frere). Confirm it is acceptable under the claims rule.
Celano, First Life 38, paraphrased: when 'and let them be lesser' was written in the rule, Francis said he wanted the fraternity called the Order of Lesser Brothers. Confirm.
Earlier Rule ch. 6: no one to be called prior, all called lesser brothers, one to wash the feet of the other; ministers as servants. Ch. 7: let them be lesser and subject to all. Confirm.
Social background of 'maiores' and 'minores' in Italian communes (including Assisi): stated as context; a historian should confirm the phrasing.
'Friars go out… begging when they must' and 'monks stay; friars move' are general summaries; confirm they are fair to both forms of religious life.
Douay-Rheims wording to confirm: Luke 22:26. 'Not long ago this path met stability' refers to day 1202 (eight days earlier); confirm 'a week ago' is acceptable or change to 'recently'.
